paragraphs: Engraving on a nineteenth century pocket pistol was a maker's advertisement as much as decoration. The work was done by hand, priced by the hour, and it is the reason surviving examples are collected as objects rather than as firearms.
The model is extremely light at 1,641 polygons and 1,780 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits historical and museum visualisation, period film and television props, collectible presentation, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The waffle iron cooks by clamping, which is why the pattern is on both sides and why the shape has barely changed since cast iron. Everything modern about it is the thermostat, and the product is still the grid.
The model is light at 57,028 polygons and 28,694 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the waffle, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits kitchen and appliance visualisation, food and e-commerce imagery, advertising, cafe and interior scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A wall of meters is what a block of flats looks like from the service side. Each one belongs to a different household, they are read by one person walking along the row, and the arrangement is the only visible evidence of how many people live behind it.
The model holds 112,785 polygons and 115,805 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 8 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits architectural and building services visualisation, utility and infrastructure presentation, urban and alley scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2018.

Televisions became furniture the moment they got thin enough to hang. The bezel disappeared, the stand became a design object, and what is on the screen matters less to the room than the black rectangle when it is off.
The model is light at 31,465 polygons and 33,893 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits interior and appliance visualisation, screen and interface mockups, e-commerce imagery, living room scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.

Sandbags work because sand does not transmit shock. Nothing about the bag matters except that it holds the fill in a shape that stacks, and the whole structure is built from a material that is free wherever it is needed.
The model holds 98,316 polygons and 95,994 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in dusty condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits military and emergency visualisation, flood defence and documentary graphics, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

An orrery is wrong on purpose. No mechanism can show both the distances and the sizes of the planets at once, so every one ever built compresses the solar system into something a room can hold and a hand can turn.
The model holds 241,249 polygons and 124,425 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in silver, and carries StemCell certification.
At $39 it suits science and education visualisation, museum and exhibition work, product and decor imagery, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

The permanent marker is one of the few office objects that is genuinely irreversible, and everybody knows it. That is why signing something with one carries weight, and why the pen is used for everything from removals to surgery.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the markers as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 the set suits product and stationery visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, office and studio scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

Blister packaging exists to be hung on a hook and to be difficult to open. The first is retail logistics, the second is theft prevention, and the customer's frustration was priced into the format from the beginning.

The model holds 46,734 polygons and 55,033 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic unbranded scheme. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits packaging design and label mockups, retail and e-commerce imagery, product visualisation, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

Modular truss is scaffolding for things that are not buildings. Stages, screens, lighting rigs and exhibition stands are all built from the same aluminium sections, bolted into whatever shape the venue and the load require.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the truss sections as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification, and further volumes of the set are offered separately.
At $38 it suits event and stage visualisation, exhibition and venue presentation, construction scenes, film and television sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Speculative control interfaces have converged on curved glass and floating panels, mostly because that reads as advanced on camera. The desk underneath is doing the real narrative work: it says somebody sits here for a long shift.
The model holds 100,690 polygons and 107,473 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $37 it suits science fiction film and animation, game environments, technology and concept presentation, exhibition work and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A mixed plate is a menu photograph rather than a dish. Different shapes, colours and thicknesses next to each other say variety before anybody reads a word, which is why the format survives on every grill menu ever printed.
The model is extremely light at 5,978 polygons and 5,166 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 it suits food and menu visualisation, restaurant and packaging imagery, advertising, kitchen and table scenes, game props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Aircraft ordnance is designed around the pylon rather than the target. The lugs, the fin spacing and the diameter are all standardised so that a squadron's stock fits any aircraft on the line, which is why they all look related.

This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the ordnance as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second volume of the set is offered separately.
At $34 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, documentary and news graphics, simulation, film props, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A contact stun device is sold on the sound it makes. The visible arc between the electrodes is a deterrent rather than a function, and most manufacturers design the discharge to be audible from several metres for exactly that reason.
The model is light at 27,829 polygons and 14,500 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in black. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits personal security and product visualisation, e-commerce imagery, film and television props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A cased compass is a precision instrument that had to survive a pocket. The lid protects the glass, the case damps the needle when closed, and every one ever made was designed on the assumption that it would be dropped.
The model is extremely light at 5,772 polygons and 3,014 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits product and outdoor visualisation, e-commerce imagery, period and expedition scenes, film props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.
